'''Michele S. Swanson''' is an American biologist who is a professor of microbiology at the [[University of Michigan]]. She has investigated the water-borne pathogen ''[[Legionella pneumophila]]''. Swanson is interested in the metabolic cues that underpin the virulence of ''L. pneumophila'' and how it is transmitted to humans. She served as president of the [[American Society for Microbiology]] from 2018-2019.<ref name=":1" />

== Early life and education ==
Swanson grew up in [[Michigan]], one of six children in her family.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Alumni Profile: Michele Swanson '82 {{!}} Yale Scientific Magazine|url=https://www.yalescientific.org/2015/11/alumni-profile-michele-swanson-82/|access-date=2021-03-22|website=www.yalescientific.org}}</ref> Her father was the first member of his family to attend university.<ref name=":0" /> Swanson spent her summer holidays playing sports at Michigan summer camps, where she played field hockey and softball. Swanson eventually earned her bachelor's degree at [[Yale University]], where she worked as a counsellor for freshmen at [[Davenport College]].<ref name=":0" /> Swanson was inspired by [[John Trinkaus]] to pursue a career in experimental biology. After graduating from Yale, Swanson joined [[Rockefeller University]] as a laboratory technician.<ref name=":0" /> She moved to [[Columbia University]] for her graduate studies, where she earned a master's degree in [[genetics]] under the supervision of [[Marian Carlson]]. Swanson joined the laboratory of [[Fred Winston]] at [[Harvard University]] where she completed her doctoral research on the interactions of various transcription factors with yeast.<ref>{{Cite thesis|title=Analysis of SPT4, SPT5, and SPT6 interactions and effects on transcription in yeast|date=1991|language=English|first=Michele Somes|last=Swanson |oclc=26072086}}</ref> She was a postdoctoral researcher at [[Tufts Medical Center]],{{citation needed|date=March 2021}} where she first became interested in ''[[Legionella pneumophila]]''.

== Research and career ==
In 1996, Swanson joined the faculty at the [[University of Michigan]].<ref name=":0" /> Swanson has studied how ''[[Legionella pneumophila]]'' remains virulent in different environments. She identified that the pathogen alternates between different cell types, one which is highly replicative and another which is highly transmissible that is primed to invade naïve hosts. After extended periods of starvation, ''L. pneumophila'' forms a highly infectious form. Swanson showed that ''L. pneumophila'' achieves these distinct cell types by coupling cellular differentiation to the metabolic state. {{citation needed|date=March 2021}}

''L. pneumophila'' can cause sporadic outbreaks of [[Legionnaires' disease]]. This was responsible for the [[Flint water crisis]] that started in 2014. Swanson has studied the mechanisms that permit ''L. pneumophila'' to persist in water, looking to create a microbiology based system to assess the safety of public water systems.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2015-09-25|title=Michele Swanson, Ph.D. {{!}} Microbiology & Immunology {{!}} Michigan Medicine|url=https://medicine.umich.edu/dept/microbiology-immunology/michele-swanson-phd|access-date=2021-03-22|website=Microbiology & Immunology|language=en}}</ref>

== Academic service ==
Swanson serves as the director of postdoctoral studies at the [[University of Michigan Medical School]] and was a part of the President's Advisory Commission on Women's Issues at the [[University of Michigan]].<ref name=":0" /> She was elected president of the [[American Society for Microbiology]] in 2018<ref>{{Cite web|date=2017-03-14|title=Michele Swanson, PhD elected President of American Society for Microbiology {{!}} Microbiology & Immunology {{!}} Michigan Medicine|url=https://medicine.umich.edu/dept/microbiology-immunology/news/archive/201703/michele-swanson-phd-elected-president-american-society-microbiology|access-date=2021-03-22|website=Microbiology & Immunology|language=en}}</ref> and hosts the ASM podcast ''This Week in Microbiology''.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=Michele Swanson, Ph.D.|url=https://asm.org/Biographies/Michele-Swanson|access-date=2021-03-22|website=ASM.org|language=en}}</ref> She was elected Fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] in 2019.<ref>{{Cite web|title=AAAS Announces Leading Scientists Elected as 2019 Fellows {{!}} American Association for the Advancement of Science|url=https://www.aaas.org/news/aaas-announces-leading-scientists-elected-2019-fellows|access-date=2021-03-22|website=www.aaas.org|language=en}}</ref>
